paragraphs: Texas Pacific Land Corporation (which, together with its subsidiaries as the context requires, may be referred to as "TPL," the "Company," "our," "we," or "us") is a Delaware Corporation and one of the largest landowners in the State of Texas with approximately 882,000 surface acres of land, principally concentrated in the Permian Basin. Additionally, we own a 1/128th nonparticipating perpetual oil and gas royalty interest ("NPRI") under approximately 85,000 acres of land, a 1/16th NPRI under approximately 371,000 acres of land, and approximately 33,000 additional net royalty acres (normalized to 1/8th) ("NRA"), for a collective total of approximately 224,000 NRA, principally concentrated in the Permian Basin.

The Company was originally organized as Texas Pacific Land Trust (the "Trust") under a Declaration of Trust, dated February 1, 1888 (the "Declaration of Trust"), to receive and hold title to extensive tracts of land in the State of Texas, previously the property of the Texas and Pacific Railway Company. The Declaration of Trust provided for the appointment of trustees (the "Trustees") to manage the assets of the Trust with all of the powers of an absolute owner. On January 11, 2021, the Trust completed its reorganization from a business trust, Texas Pacific Land Trust, into Texas Pacific Land Corporation, a corporation formed and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware (the "Corporate Reorganization").

Our surface and royalty ownership provide revenue opportunities throughout the oil and gas development value chain. While we are not an oil and gas producer, we benefit from various revenue sources throughout the life cycle of a well. During the initial development phase whereby infrastructure for oil and gas development is constructed, we receive fixed fee payments for use of our land and revenue for sales of materials (caliche) used in the construction of the infrastructure. During the drilling and completion phase, we generate revenue by providing sourced water and/or treated produced water as well as fixed fee payments from the use of our land and revenue related to the sale of sand to operators. During the production phase, we receive revenue from our oil and gas royalty interests and revenue related to saltwater disposal on our land. In addition, we generate revenue from pipeline, power line and utility easements, commercial leases and temporary permits principally related to a variety of land uses, including, but not limited to, midstream infrastructure projects and processing facilities as hydrocarbons are processed and transported to market. Additionally, as a result of an acquisition in 2024, we receive commercial revenue related to land leased to a third party that operates a nonhazardous oilfield solids waste disposal site.

Our mission is to pursue a thoughtful, long-term approach towards optimizing and building upon the commercial and environmental virtues of our extensive lands and resources. We have a long history of responsible management of our legacy assets, and since 2016, we have expanded our business strategy to generate incremental revenue streams that take advantage of our vast surface and royalty footprint, such as our investments in the Water Services and Operations business segment. Beyond our core businesses, we continue to explore new opportunities related to renewable energy, environmental sustainability, and technology, among others, that can leverage our existing legacy surface and royalty assets. For example, in December 2025, we invested $50.0 million in a strategic agreement with a data and energy infrastructure company. See further discussion below

under "Recent Developments." Our business model emphasizes high cash flow margins and relatively low ongoing capital expenditure requirements, and we expect new opportunities to generally align with these priorities. We remain focused on optimizing long-term value creation and profitability, fostering responsible stewardship of our assets, providing quality customer service, and engaging with and advocating for employee and stakeholder interests.

On October 23, 2025, we entered into a credit agreement with Wells Fargo Bank, National Association and certain other lenders (collectively the "Lenders"), which provides for a revolving credit facility (the "Credit Facility") in the aggregate principal amount of up to $500.0 million. The Credit Facility includes the ability to request potential increases in the commitments of the Lenders of up to an additional $250.0 million; provided that any such request for an increase must be in a minimum amount of $50.0 million or, if less, the remaining available capacity for such increases. The Credit Facility and all borrowings thereunder will mature on October 23, 2029. Borrowings under the Credit Facility will generally bear interest at the Secured Overnight Financing Rate ("SOFR") plus 2.25% to 2.50% based on our consolidated total leverage ratio. The Credit Facility is initially unsecured, with a springing security interest in substantially all equity securities of our subsidiaries in the event our consolidated total leverage ratio exceeds 2.50 to 1.0. The Credit Facility also contains customary financial and other affirmative and negative covenants and events of default. No draws were made under the Credit Facility during 2025, and the Credit Facility remained undrawn as of the date of this Annual Report.

On December 22, 2025, we effected a three-for-one stock split of our common stock, par value $0.01 per share ("Common Stock"), and trading began on a stock split adjusted basis on December 23, 2025. Unless the context otherwise requires, all share and per share information (including information regarding treasury shares, restricted stock awards ("RSAs"), restricted stock units ("RSUs"), and performance stock units ("PSUs")) has been retroactively adjusted to reflect the stock split. The par value of Common Stock was not affected by the stock split and remains at $0.01 per share. Accordingly, an amount equal to the par value of the increased shares resulting from the stock split was reclassified from "Additional paid-in capital" to "Common Stock" on our consolidated balance sheets.
We completed the following asset acquisitions during 2025:
•In March 2025, we acquired 177 NRA located primarily in the Midland Basin for an aggregate purchase price of $3.5 million, net of post-closing adjustments, in an all-cash transaction.
•In May 2025, we acquired 787 acres of land in Reeves County, Texas for an aggregate purchase price, inclusive of closing costs, of $4.5 million in an all-cash transaction.
•In September 2025, we acquired 8,147 acres of land in Martin County, Texas for an aggregate purchase price, inclusive of closing costs, of $31.4 million in an all-cash transaction.

•In November 2025, we acquired 17,306 NRA located primarily in the Midland Basin in Martin, Howard, Midland, and other counties for an aggregate purchase price of $450.7 million, net of post-closing adjustments, in an all-cash transaction.

In December 2025, we made a minority investment of $50.0 million in Bolt Data & Energy, Inc. ("Bolt") pursuant to a strategic agreement to develop and enable large scale data center campuses and supporting infrastructure across our land. Bolt is a data energy infrastructure company co-founded by Eric Schmidt, former CEO and Chairman of Google, who also serves as Bolt's Chairman. As part of the agreement, Bolt raised $150.0 million of capital inclusive of our $50.0 million investment. In connection with our investment, we received an equity interest, warrants, and a right of first refusal to supply water to Bolt-affiliated projects and related infrastructure. Additionally, the terms of the agreement provide an opportunity for the Company to contribute land to Bolt in exchange for additional Bolt equity subject to mutual agreement by both parties. Bolt is currently pursuing commercial partnerships and anchor customers to develop large-scale data centers on our land.

We operate our business in two reportable segments: Land and Resource Management and Water Services and Operations. Our segments provide management with a comprehensive financial view of our key businesses. Our segments enable the alignment of strategies and objectives of the Company and provide a framework for timely and rational allocation of resources within businesses. See Part II, Item 7. "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and Note 16, "Business Segment Reporting" in the notes to our consolidated financial statements included under Part II, Item 8. "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data."

paragraphs: An investment in our securities involves a degree of risk. The risks described below, and other risks noted throughout this Annual Report, including those risks identified in Part II, Item 7. "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," are not the only ones facing us. Additional risks not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also have a material adverse effect on us. If any of the following risks actually occur, our financial condition, results of operations, cash flows or business could be harmed. In that case, the market price of our stock could decline and you could lose part or all of your investment in our stock.

The oil and gas royalties that we receive are dependent upon the market prices for oil and gas, and decreases in such prices for oil and gas negatively impact the revenue realized on our oil and gas royalties. Reductions in market prices for oil and gas could also lead to decreased exploration and development activity by the operators of the properties on which we own oil and gas royalty interests, which could reduce our revenue potential with respect to such interests. Market prices for oil and gas are subject to U.S. and global macroeconomic and geopolitical conditions and infrastructure and logistical constraints, amongst others, and, in the past, have been subject to significant price fluctuations. Price fluctuations for oil and gas have been particularly volatile in recent years due to supply and demand factors, worldwide energy conservation measures, OPEC and OPEC+ actions, global conflicts in major oil producing regions, especially in Eastern Europe and the Middle East, and general economic cycles, among other factors. These events and conditions have, at times, resulted in a reduction of global economic activity and volatility in the global financial markets. The scale and duration of the impact of these factors remain unknowable but could lead to a decrease in our revenues and have a material impact on our business segments and earnings, cash flow and financial condition.

We are not an oil and gas producer. Our oil and gas royalty revenue is derived primarily from perpetual non-participating oil and gas royalty interests that we have retained or oil and gas interests that we have acquired. As oil and gas wells age, their production capacity may decline absent additional investment. However, the owners and operators of the oil and gas wells make all decisions as to investments in, and production from, those wells and our royalties are dependent upon decisions made by those owners and operators, among other factors. Accordingly, a significant portion of our revenues is reliant on the management and actions of third parties, over whom we have no control. Such third parties may not take actions or make decisions that will be beneficial to us, which could result in adverse effects on our financial results and performance.

Our estimated proved developed producing ("PDP") reserves are based on many assumptions that may prove to be inaccurate. Any inaccuracies in these estimates or underlying assumptions may materially affect the quantities and present value of our reserves.

It is not possible to measure underground accumulations of oil, gas, and NGL with precision. Oil and gas reserve engineering requires subjective estimates of underground accumulations of oil and gas and assumptions concerning future oil and gas prices, production levels, ultimate recoveries and operating and development costs. In estimating our PDP reserves, we and Ryder Scott Company, L.P. ("Ryder Scott"), an independent third-party petroleum engineering firm, must make various assumptions with respect to many matters that may prove to be incorrect, including:
•future oil, gas, and NGL prices; •unexpected complications from offset well development; •production rates;

headings: Year Ended December 31, 2025 Compared to Year Ended December 31, 2024
paragraphs: The following Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operation ("MD&A") is intended to help the reader understand the results of operations and financial condition of Texas Pacific Land Corporation. MD&A is provided as a supplement to, and should be read in conjunction with, our consolidated financial statements and the accompanying notes to financial statements included in Part II, Item 8. of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. This discussion and analysis contains forward-looking statements that involve risks, uncertainties and assumptions. Actual results may differ materially from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements as a result of various factors, including, but not limited to, those factors presented in Part I, Item 1A. "Risk Factors" and elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. This section generally discusses the results of our operations for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the year ended December 31, 2024. For a discussion of the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to the year ended December 31, 2023, refer to Part II, Item 7. "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024.

TPL was originally organized in 1888 as a business trust to hold title to extensive tracts of land in the State of Texas that were previously the property of the Texas and Pacific Railway Company. On January 11, 2021, we completed our Corporate Reorganization from a business trust to a corporation and changed our name from Texas Pacific Land Trust to Texas Pacific Land Corporation.

Our business activity is generated from our surface and royalty interest ownership, primarily in the Permian Basin. Our revenues are derived from oil and gas royalties, water sales, produced water royalties, easements and other surface-related income and land sales. Due to the nature of our operations and concentration of our ownership in one geographic location, our revenue and net income are subject to substantial fluctuations from quarter to quarter and year to year. In addition to fluctuations in response to changes in the market price for oil and gas, our financial results are subject to decisions by not only the owners and operators of oil and gas wells to which our oil and gas royalty interests relate, but also to other owners and operators in the Permian Basin as it relates to our other revenue streams, principally water sales, produced water royalties, easements and other surface-related revenue.

Average West Texas Intermediate ("WTI") oil prices for the year ended December 31, 2025 were down approximately 15% compared to average WTI oil prices during the same period last year. Oil prices continue to be impacted by certain actions by OPEC+, geopolitics, and evolving global supply and demand trends, among other factors. In addition, ambiguity around tariffs implemented by and towards the United States has created incremental global economic uncertainty, which, in part, contributed to relatively weaker oil prices in 2025. Average Henry Hub natural gas prices during 2025 increased approximately 61% compared to average prior year natural gas prices. Global and domestic natural gas markets benefited in 2025 from improved supply-demand balances, including tailwinds from expanded liquefied natural gas capacity and improved industrial and power demand, among other factors. Since mid-2022, the Waha Hub located in Pecos County, Texas has at times experienced significant negative price differentials relative to Henry Hub, located in Erath, Louisiana, due in part to growing local Permian natural gas production and limited natural gas pipeline takeaway capacity. Midstream infrastructure is currently being developed by operators to provide additional takeaway capacity, though the impact on future basis differentials will be dependent on future natural gas production and other factors. Changes in global and domestic macro-economic conditions could result in additional shifts in oil and gas supply and demand in future periods. Although our revenues are directly and indirectly impacted by oil and natural gas prices, we believe our royalty interests (which require no capital expenditures or operating expense burden from us for well development), strong balance sheet, and liquidity position will help us navigate through potential commodity price volatility.

As the largest oil producing shale basin in the world, the Permian depends on large-scale water solutions related to well development and produced water disposal. For oil and gas well development, often hundreds of thousands of barrels of water are required per well completion. To enhance productivity and drilling economics, oil and gas operators have generally expanded the amount of water per well completion and reduced the time to complete a well. These factors have led to intensifying demands for completion water delivery and assurance, which generally benefits completion water providers with larger size and scale. We believe we have a competitive advantage in this market with our significant surface footprint and a large network of owned and operated water wells, storage ponds, recycling assets, and pipelines that can source and deliver water to customers throughout the Permian.

Permian produced water volumes have grown commensurately with overall Permian oil production. Though some produced water is reused and recycled for completion activities, the majority of Permian produced water is injected into subsurface pore space via saltwater disposal wells. Saltwater disposal availability varies throughout the Permian depending on regulations, permitted injected rates, and the availability of pore space and infrastructure. Our extensive land holdings contain and are adjacent to extensive pore space, and, through various commercial agreements, we allow produced water operators to transport and dispose of produced water across our surface footprint. Furthermore, our previously mentioned desalination project could potentially provide an additional solution for produced water by reducing the amount of water required to be injected subsurface.

The Permian Basin is one of the oldest and most well-known hydrocarbon-producing areas and currently accounts for a substantial portion of oil and gas production in the United States, covering approximately 86,000 square miles in 52 counties across southeastern New Mexico and western Texas. Exploration and production ("E&P") companies active in the Permian generally decreased their drilling and development activity in 2025 compared to recent prior year activity levels in response to lower oil prices. Despite relatively lower activity, Permian production, per the U.S. Energy Information Administration ("EIA"), averaged approximately 6.5 million barrels of oil per day during 2025.

Due to our ownership concentration in the Permian Basin, our revenues are directly impacted by oil and gas pricing and drilling activity in the Permian Basin. headings: 營業收入佔總額百分比
paragraphs: Texas Pacific Land Corporation (which, together with its subsidiaries as the context requires, may be referred to as "TPL," the "Company," "our," "we," or "us") 是一家 Delaware 公司，為德克薩斯州最大的土地所有者之一，擁有約 882,000 英畝地表土地，主要集中在 Permian Basin。此外，我們擁有約 85,000 英畝土地的 1/128 非參與性永續油氣租權 ("NPRI")，約 371,000 英畝土地的 1/16 非參與性永續油氣租權，以及約 33,000 增加的淨租權英畝（換算為 1/8 面積）("NRA")，總計約 224,000 NRA，主要集中在 Permian Basin。

本公司最初成立為 Texas Pacific Land Trust (the "Trust")，根據 1888 年 2 月 1 日簽訂的信託聲明 (the "Declaration of Trust")，用以接收並持有德克薩斯州廣大土地的所有權，這些土地原先屬於 Texas and Pacific Railway Company。信託聲明規定任命信託人 (the "Trustees") 管理信託資產，並擁有絕對所有權的全部權力。2021 年 1 月 11 日，信託完成從 Texas Pacific Land Trust 這個商業信託轉型為 Texas Pacific Land Corporation，一家根據德克薩斯州法律成立並運作的公司 (the "Corporate Reorganization")。

我們的地表與租權所有權提供油氣開發價值鏈中的收入機會。雖然我們不是油氣生產者，但我們在油氣井的全生命週期中可從多種收入來源受益。在初始開發階段，當建設油氣開發基礎設施時，我們會因使用我們的土地而獲得固定費用，並因銷售用於基礎設施建設的材料 (caliche) 而獲得收入。在鑽井與完井階段，我們透過提供來源水與/或處理後的產出水，以及因使用我們的土地而獲得固定費用，並因銷售砩砂給運營商而獲得收入。在生產階段，我們會因油氣租權而獲得收入，並因在土地上處理鹽水而獲得收入。此外，我們還會因管線、電力線與公用設施的通行權、商業租賃與臨時許可而獲得收入，這些主要與多種土地用途相關，包括但不僅限於中游基礎設施項目與處理設施，用以處理與運輸石化產品至市場。此外，因 2024 年的收購，我們也會因將土地出租給第三方運營非危險性油氣固體廢棄物處理場而獲得商業收入。

我們的使命是追求一種深思熟慮、長遠的策略，以優化並拓展我們廣大土地與資源的商業與環境價值。我們有長久的責任管理我們的遺產資產的歷史，自 2016 年起，我們已擴展業務策略，以產生額外的收入來源，利用我們廣大的地表與租權版圖，例如我們在 Water Services and Operations 商業分部的投資。除了核心業務外，我們持續探索與可再生能源、環境永續性與科技等相關的新機會，這些機會可以利用我們現有的遺產地表與租權資產。例如，在 2025 年 12 月，我們與一家數據與能源基礎設施公司簽訂戰略協議，投資 5,000 萬美元。詳見以下 "Recent Developments" 部分的進一步討論。
我們的商業模式強調高現金流毛利率與相對低的持續資本支出需求，我們預期新的機會通常會與這些優先事項一致。我們持續專注於優化長期價值創造與利潤率，促進我們資產的負責任管理，提供優質客戶服務，並與員工與股東利益相關者進行溝通與倡導。

2025 年 10 月 23 日，我們與 Wells Fargo Bank, National Association 及其他貸款人 (collectively the "Lenders") 籤訂信貸協議，提供總計最高 5 億美元的循環信貸融資 (the "Credit Facility")。信貸融資包括貸款人可能增加信貸額度的潛在權利，最高額度為額外 2.5 億美元；但任何增加信貸額度的請求必須至少為 5,000 萬美元，或若較低，則為該增加額度的剩餘可用容量。信貸融資及其下所有貸款將於 2029 年 10 月 23 日到期。信貸融資下的貸款將通常以 Secured Overnight Financing Rate ("SOFR") 加上 2.25% 到 2.50% 的利率計算，利率根據我們的合併總負債比率而定。信貸融資最初為無擔保，若我們的合併總負債比率超過 2.50 到 1.0，則會啟動對我們子公司所有股權證券的擔保權益。信貸融資也包含常見的財務與其他正面與負面契約條款與違約事件。2025 年期間，信貸融資未有提款，且截至本年度報告日，信貸融資仍為未提款。

2025 年 12 月 22 日，我們執行了我們普通股的三股換一股的股票分割，每股面值為 0.01 美元 ("Common Stock")，並於 2025 年 12 月 23 日開始以股票分割調整後的基礎進行交易。除非上下文另有要求，所有股數與每股資訊（包括有關庫藏股、限制性股票獎勵 ("RSAs"), 限制性股票單位 ("RSUs"), 以及績效股票單位 ("PSUs") 的資訊）均已追溯調整以反映股票分割。普通股的面值未因股票分割而改變，仍為每股 0.01 美元。因此，股票分割後增加的股份面值金額已從 "額外資本" 調整至 "普通股"，反映在我們的合併資產負債表中。
我們在 2025 年完成了以下資產收購：
•民國114年3月，本公司以現金交易取得位於Midland Basin主要地區的177筆NRA，總購置價格為350萬美元，扣除交割後調整後的金額。
•民國114年5月，本公司以現金交易取得位於Texas Reeves County的787英畝土地，總購置價格包含交割費用為450萬美元。
•民國114年9月，本公司以現金交易取得位於Texas Martin County的8,147英畝土地，總購置價格包含交割費用為3,140萬美元。
•民國114年11月，本公司以現金交易取得位於Martin、Howard、Midland及其他縣市的Midland Basin主要地區的17,306筆NRA，總購置價格為4.507億美元，扣除交割後調整後的金額。

民國114年12月，本公司根據戰略協議，對Bolt Data & Energy, Inc.（"Bolt"）進行少數投資，投資金額為5,000萬美元。Bolt為一數據能源基礎設施公司，由Eric Schmidt創辦，他曾擔任Google的CEO與董事長，現為Bolt的董事長。根據協議，Bolt已籌集1.5億美元資金，包含本公司的5,000萬美元投資。根據投資協議，本公司取得Bolt的股權、選擇權，以及優先供應水資源給Bolt相關專案與基礎設施的權利。此外，協議條款亦提供本公司在雙方同意的情況下，以土地換取Bolt額外股權的機會。目前Bolt正積極尋求商業合作夥伴與主要客戶，以在本公司土地上開發大型資料中心。
本公司營運業務分為兩個應報告分部：土地與資源管理及水服務與營運。這些分部為管理層提供完整的財務視圖，以掌握本公司的關鍵業務。這些分部有助於本公司策略與目標的對齊，並提供資源在業務內進行及時且合理的配置框架。請參閱本年度財務報表附註第16項「業務分部報告」，以及財務報表附註第II項第7項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析」及第II項第8項「財務報表與補充資料」。

關鍵會計政策與會計估計
paragraphs: 以下為管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之分析（"MD&A"），旨在協助讀者瞭解德州太平洋土地公司（Texas Pacific Land Corporation）之營運結果與財務狀況。MD&A為財務報表之補充說明，應與我們之合併財務報表及財務報表附註一同閱讀，包含於本年度10-K申報表第二部分，第8項。此討論與分析包含前瞻性陳述，涉及風險、不確定性與假設。實際結果可能與這些前瞻性陳述所預期者有重大差異，原因可能包括但不限於第一部分，第1A項所列之風險因素及其他處於本年度10-K申報表中所述因素。本節一般討論我們於2025年12月31日為結算日之營運結果，與2024年12月31日為結算日之比較。如需瞭解2024年12月31日為結算日與2023年12月31日為結算日之比較，請參閱我們2024年度10-K申報表第二部分，第7項 "管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之分析"。
TPL最初於1888年成立為一個商業信託，用以持有德克薩斯州廣大土地的所有權，這些土地原先屬於德州與太平洋鐵路公司。我們於2021年1月11日完成從商業信託轉為公司的企業重整，並將公司名稱由德州太平洋土地信託（Texas Pacific Land Trust）更名為德州太平洋土地公司（Texas Pacific Land Corporation）。

我們的營運活動主要來自於我們對地表與礦權權益之擁有，主要集中於佩恩盆地（Permian Basin）。我們的收入來自於石油與天然氣礦權收益、水銷售、產出水礦權收益、權利金與其他地表相關收入以及土地銷售。由於我們營運的性質與地緣集中於單一地理區域，我們的收入與淨收入會因季節與年度而有顯著波動。除了市場價格變動對油氣價格的影響外，我們的財務結果亦受到油氣井所有者與經營者之決定影響，包括與我們其他收入來源相關的其他所有者與經營者，特別是水銷售、產出水礦權收益、權利金與其他地表相關收入。

2025年12月31日結算年度之平均西德克薩斯中間價（"WTI"）石油價格，與去年同期相比下降約15%。石油價格持續受到OPEC+之行動、地緣政治以及全球供應與需求趨勢等多種因素影響。此外，美國所實施之關稅措施的不確定性，也造成全球經濟的不確定性，部分導致2025年石油價格相對較弱。2025年平均亨利中心（Henry Hub）天然氣價格相比去年同期提高約61%。2025年全球與國內天然氣市場受益於供應與需求的改善，包括液化天然氣容量擴張與工業與電力需求改善等因素。自2022年中以來，位於德克薩斯州佩科斯縣的瓦哈中心（Waha Hub）時常出現相對於亨利中心（位於路易斯安那州埃拉特）的負價格差異，部分原因在於當地佩恩盆地天然氣生產增加與天然氣輸送管線容量有限。目前中游基礎設施正由運營商開發以增加輸送容量，但未來價格差異的影響將取決於未來天然氣生產及其他因素。全球與國內總體經濟條件的變化可能導致未來期間油氣供應與需求的進一步變動。雖然我們的收入直接與間接受到油氣價格的影響，我們認為我們的礦權權益（無需我們投入資本支出或營運費用）、強固的資產負債表與流動性地位，將幫助我們應對潛在的能源價格波動。

作為全球最大的油氣頁巖盆地，佩恩盆地依賴大量水資源用於鑽井開發與產出水處理。於油氣鑽井開發中，通常每口井需要數十萬桶的水。為提高生產效率與鑽井經濟效益，油氣運營商已普遍增加每口井的用水量並縮短鑽井時間。這些因素導致對完井用水供應與保障的需求持續增加，通常對規模較大的完井用水供應商較為有利。我們認為我們在這個市場中擁有競爭優勢，因為我們擁有廣大的地表權益與大量自有與運營的用水井、儲水池、回收設施與輸送管道，可為客戶提供全佩恩盆地範圍內的用水供應。

佩恩盆地的產出水量隨著整體油氣生產量同步增長。雖然部分產出水被重複使用與回收用於完井活動，但大多數佩恩盆地的產出水是透過鹽水處理井注入地下孔隙空間。鹽水處理的可用性根據佩恩盆地的規範、允許注入速率與孔隙空間與基礎設施的可用性而有所不同。我們廣大的土地權益包含並鄰近廣大的孔隙空間，透過多種商業協議，我們允許產出水運營商在我們的地表權益範圍內運輸與處理產出水。此外，我們先前提及的海水淡化專案，可能提供另一種解決方案，透過減少需注入地下的水量。
佩恩盆地是世界上最古老且最知名的氫碳化合物生產區之一，目前佔美國油氣生產的相當大比例，涵蓋約86,000平方英里，橫跨新墨西哥州東南部與德克薩斯州西部的52個縣。在佩恩盆地從事探勘與生產（"E&P"）的公司，通常因油價較低而在2025年減少鑽井與開發活動，與近期前一年的活動水平相比。儘管活動較低，根據美國能源資訊管理局（"EIA"）的數據，2025年佩恩盆地的生產量平均約為每天650萬桶油。
由於我們在佩恩盆地的權益集中，我們的收入直接受到佩恩盆地油氣價格與鑽井活動的影響。以下指標顯示2025年12月31日與2024年12月31日結算年度的佩恩盆地部分油氣價格與活動水平：

headings: 與本公司業務相關的風險
本公司油氣租權收入依賴於油氣市場價格，而市場價格會波動。
本公司並非油氣生產者。本公司來自油氣租權的收入取決於其他方的行動。
本公司管理團隊關鍵成員流失或難以吸引並留住經驗豐富的技術人員，可能會降低本公司競爭力與未來成功前景。
TPWR 產品與服務的需求大幅取決於客戶的支出水平。
本公司在 TPWR 新興且快速發展的市場中進行業務，面臨相關風險，可能無法成功應對這些風險，並達到可接受的成功程度或利潤水平。
政府對 TPWR 的規範影響可能會對本公司業務產生不利影響。
本公司生產水脫鹽專案會產生與投入資本、環境風險及本公司聲譽相關的風險。
本公司銷售土地所產生的營業收入易受顯著波動。土地銷售受許多超出本公司控制範圍的因素影響。
本公司之信用貸款協議可能限制本公司營運彈性，或以其他方式對本公司業務產生不利影響。
本公司可能進行少數股權投資、參與合資企業或與第三方簽訂其他戰略聯盟，此等行為可能使本公司面臨超出本公司控制範圍之風險與不確定性。
與本公司普通股相關之風險
本公司普通股之市場價格可能出現顯著波動。
本公司可能無法持續發放股息，或發放之股息率可能低於先前之發放率。
本公司將評估未來是否購回現有普通股，且無法保證購回股份之時機或數量，若有購回則亦無保證。
本公司未來發行額外普通股將導致其他股東之持股比例被稀釋。
州法及反收購條款可能使我們的董事會能抵禦第三方的收購嘗試，並限制我們股東的權力。
與我們產業相關的風險
我們的業務及財務結果可能因超出我們控制範圍的自然或人為因素而受到幹擾。
我們的業務及財務結果受產業重大趨勢影響，例如減碳，並可能因超出我們控制範圍的未來發展而受到不利影響。
我們的業務可能因激進投資者行動而受到負面影響。
paragraphs: 投資本公司證券涉及一定風險。下列所描述的風險，以及本年度報告中其他部分所提及的風險，包括 Part II, Item 7. "管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之分析" 所識別的風險，並非唯一可能影響本公司的風險。尚有其他風險，目前本公司尚未知悉或認為不重要，但這些風險也可能對本公司造成重大不利影響。若任何上述風險實際發生，將可能對本公司財務狀況、營運結果、現金流量或業務造成損害。在這種情況下，本公司股票的市場價格可能下跌，您可能損失部分或全部投資於本公司股票的金額。

我們所收取的石油與天然氣租金收入，取決於石油與天然氣的市場價格，而石油與天然氣價格的下降會對我們的石油與天然氣租金收入造成負面影響。石油與天然氣市場價格的下降也可能導致石油與天然氣產權所有者與經營者減少對其產權的探勘與開發活動，進而降低我們對這些產權的收入潛力。石油與天然氣的市場價格受到美國與全球總體經濟與地緣政治條件，以及基礎建設與物流限制等因素的影響，過去也曾經歷顯著的價格波動。近年來，石油與天然氣的價格波動尤其顯著，這是因為供應與需求因素、全球能源節約措施、OPEC 與 OPEC+ 的行動、主要石油生產地區的全球衝突，特別是在東歐與中東地區，以及一般經濟週期等因素所致。這些事件與條件有時會導致全球經濟活動減少與全球金融市場的波動。這些因素的規模與持續時間目前無法預測，但可能導致我們收入減少，並對我們的業務分部與獲利、現金流量與財務狀況造成重大影響。

本公司並非石油與天然氣生產商。我們的石油與天然氣租金收入主要來自於我們保留或取得的永續非參與石油與天然氣租金權益。隨著石油與天然氣井的使用年限增加，其產能可能下降，除非進行額外投資。然而，石油與天然氣井的所有者與經營者會做出所有關於這些井的投資與生產決策，而我們的租金收入則取決於這些所有者與經營者的決策，以及其他因素。因此，我們收入的很大一部分取決於第三方的管理與行動，而我們對這些第三方毫無控制權。這些第三方可能不會採取對我們有益的行動或做出決策，這可能會對我們的財務結果與表現造成不利影響。
我們預估的已開發生產井（"PDP"）儲備量是基於許多假設，這些假設可能證明是不正確的。任何這些估計值或基礎假設的不準確性都可能對我們的儲備量數量與現值造成重大影響。
無法精確測量地下油、氣與 NGL 的儲量。油氣儲備工程需要對地下油氣儲量做出主觀估計，並假設未來油氣價格、生產量、最終回收率與營運與開發成本。在估計我們的 PDP 儲備時，我們與 Ryder Scott Company, L.P.（"Ryder Scott"），一家獨立的第三方石油工程公司，必須就許多事項做出各種假設，這些假設可能證明是錯誤的，包括：
•未來油、氣與 NGL 價格；•來自鄰井開發的意外複雜情況；•生產速率；
